speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the exposure to a sibling with recent chickenpox and the presence of painless, nonpruritic papules, I suspect a related herpesvirus infection. To confirm this, I need to see the characteristic appearance of the lesions. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pearly, umbilicated papules is classic for Molluscum contagiosum, which is common in daycare settings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
